data.solver: pinneapple_design.aero.panel.panel_solve (Hess-Smith), Cp on the panel mid-points

transolver.name: transolver
transolver.source: Wu et al., 'Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries', ICML 2024 (arXiv:2402.02366)
transolver.note: physics-attention: every point is softly assigned to learned slices, attention runs on the slices, the result is scattered back. Cost O(N M + M^2), so it scales to the tens of thousands of surface points of a car. The library's implementation is pinneapple_neural.architectures.neural_operators.transolver and is wrapped, not reimplemented.

pointnet.name: pointnet
pointnet.source: Qi et al., 'PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation', CVPR 2017 (arXiv:1612.00593)
pointnet.note: shared per-point MLP, a global max pool, and the pooled code concatenated back to every point. The cheap baseline: no geometric message passing, so it is the row that shows what the attention buys.

gino.name: gino
gino.source: Li et al., 'Geometry-Informed Neural Operator for Large-Scale 3D PDEs' (GINO), NeurIPS 2023 (arXiv:2309.00583)
gino.note: OPEN. A graph encoder, a Fourier neural operator on a latent regular grid and a graph decoder. It needs a regridding step (the FNO part sees a grid, the geometry arrives as a graph) and the reference implementation pulls in torch-scatter and torch-geometric, which the library does not depend on. The interface here already carries what it needs — arbitrary points, per-point normals, a variable count — so a GINO backend implements the same three methods and nothing else changes.

meshgraphnet.name: meshgraphnet
meshgraphnet.source: Pfaff et al., 'Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks', ICLR 2021 (arXiv:2010.03409)
meshgraphnet.note: ALREADY IN THE LIBRARY, not wrapped here: pinneapple_neural.architectures.graphnn.MeshGraphNet (with #236's world-space edges) is the baseline the aero app runs. It is a fixed-topology model — it learns on the edges of one mesh — so putting it behind this interface would mean either re-triangulating every shape to a common connectivity (which is a different promise: 'geometry-agnostic' would become 'one topology') or rebuilding the graph per shape. Both are reasonable; neither is done, and wrapping it badly would make the comparison dishonest. It stays the reference row of the benchmark, trained on the shared mesh.
